audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Samaritan woman, living water, worship in Spirit/truth, I am saying, harvest, Samaritan belief, and royal official's son.

verses.restored: When therefore Jesus knew that the Pharisees heard Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John,

familiar.text: When therefore the LORD knew how the Pharisees had heard that Jesus made and baptized more disciples than John,

modern.text: When Jesus realized that the Pharisees were aware He was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John

original.text: Ὡς οὖν ἔγνω ὁ ⸀Ἰησοῦς ὅτι ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὅτι Ἰησοῦς πλείονας μαθητὰς ποιεῖ καὶ βαπτίζει ἢ Ἰωάννης—

verses.restored: though Jesus himself was not baptizing, but his disciples,

familiar.text: (Though Jesus himself baptized not, but his disciples,)

modern.text: (although it was not Jesus who baptized, but His disciples),

original.text: καίτοιγε Ἰησοῦς αὐτὸς οὐκ ἐβάπτιζεν ἀλλʼ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ—

verses.restored: he left Judea and went away again into Galilee.

familiar.text: He left Judaea, and departed again into Galilee.

modern.text: He left Judea and returned to Galilee.

original.text: ἀφῆκεν τὴν Ἰουδαίαν καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ⸀πάλιν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.

verses.restored: It was necessary for him to pass through Samaria.

familiar.text: And he must needs go through Samaria.

modern.text: Now He had to pass through Samaria.

original.text: ἔδει δὲ αὐτὸν διέρχεσθαι διὰ τῆς Σαμαρείας.

verses.restored: He comes therefore to a city of Samaria called Sychar, near the field Jacob had given to Joseph his son.

familiar.text: Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.

modern.text: So He came to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.

original.text: ἔρχεται οὖν εἰς πόλιν τῆς Σαμαρείας λεγομένην Συχὰρ πλησίον τοῦ χωρίου ὃ ἔδωκεν Ἰακὼβ ⸀τῷ Ἰωσὴφ τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ·

verses.restored: Jacob's well was there. Jesus, wearied from the journey, was sitting thus by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

familiar.text: Now Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour.

modern.text: Since Jacob’s well was there, Jesus, weary from His journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

original.text: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ πηγὴ τοῦ Ἰακώβ. ὁ οὖν Ἰησοῦς κεκοπιακὼς ἐκ τῆς ὁδοιπορίας ἐκαθέζετο οὕτως ἐπὶ τῇ πηγῇ· ὥρα ἦν ⸀ὡς ἕκτη.

verses.restored: A woman from Samaria comes to draw water. Jesus says to her, Give me to drink.

familiar.text: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.

modern.text: When a Samaritan woman came to draw water, Jesus said to her, “Give Me a drink.”

original.text: Ἔρχεται γυνὴ ἐκ τῆς Σαμαρείας ἀντλῆσαι ὕδωρ. λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Δός μοι πεῖν·

verses.restored: For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.

familiar.text: (For his disciples were gone away unto the city to buy meat.)

modern.text: (His disciples had gone into the town to buy food.)

original.text: οἱ γὰρ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἀπεληλύθεισαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἵνα τροφὰς ἀγοράσωσιν.

verses.restored: The Samaritan woman says to him, How is it that you, being a Judean, ask a drink from me, being a Samaritan woman? For Judeans do not share vessels with Samaritans.

familiar.text: Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.

modern.text: “You are a Jew,” said the woman. “How can You ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews do not associate with Samaritans.)

original.text: λέγει οὖν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ ἡ Σαμαρῖτις· Πῶς σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὢν παρʼ ἐμοῦ πεῖν αἰτεῖς ⸂γυναικὸς Σαμαρίτιδος οὔσης⸃; οὐ γὰρ συγχρῶνται Ἰουδαῖοι Σαμαρίταις.

verses.restored: Jesus answered and said to her, If you knew the gift of the Divine and who it is saying to you, Give me to drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.

familiar.text: Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “If you knew the gift of God and who is asking you for a drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Εἰ ᾔδεις τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ λέγων σοι· Δός μοι πεῖν, σὺ ἂν ᾔτησας αὐτὸν καὶ ἔδωκεν ἄν σοι ὕδωρ ζῶν.

verses.restored: She says to him, Lord, you have no bucket, and the well is deep; from where then do you have the living water?

familiar.text: The woman saith unto him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: from whence then hast thou that living water?

modern.text: “Sir,” the woman replied, “You have nothing to draw with and the well is deep. Where then will You get this living water?

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ⸂ἡ γυνή⸃· Κύριε, οὔτε ἄντλημα ἔχεις καὶ τὸ φρέαρ ἐστὶν βαθύ· πόθεν οὖν ἔχεις τὸ ὕδωρ τὸ ζῶν;

verses.restored: Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, and his sons and his livestock?

familiar.text: Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle?

modern.text: Are You greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well and drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock?”

original.text: μὴ σὺ μείζων εἶ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἰακώβ, ὃς ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν τὸ φρέαρ καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔπιεν καὶ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰ θρέμματα αὐτοῦ;

verses.restored: Jesus answered and said to her, Everyone drinking from this water will thirst again.

familiar.text: Jesus answered and said unto her, Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again:

modern.text: Jesus said to her, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Πᾶς ὁ πίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος τούτου διψήσει πάλιν·

verses.restored: But whoever drinks from the water that I will give will certainly not thirst into the age; but the water that I will give will become in that one a spring of water leaping up into age-long life.

familiar.text: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.

modern.text: But whoever drinks the water I give him will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life.”

original.text: ὃς δʼ ἂν πίῃ ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος οὗ ἐγὼ δώσω αὐτῷ, οὐ μὴ ⸀διψήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ τὸ ὕδωρ ὃ δώσω αὐτῷ γενήσεται ἐν αὐτῷ πηγὴ ὕδατος ἁλλομένου εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

verses.restored: The woman says to him, Lord, give me this water, so that I may not thirst nor come here to draw.

familiar.text: The woman saith unto him, Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come hither to draw.

modern.text: The woman said to Him, “Sir, give me this water so that I will not get thirsty and have to keep coming here to draw water.”

original.text: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνή· Κύριε, δός μοι τοῦτο τὸ ὕδωρ, ἵνα μὴ διψῶ μηδὲ ⸀διέρχωμαι ἐνθάδε ἀντλεῖν.

verses.restored: He says to her, Go, call your husband and come here.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither.

modern.text: Jesus told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.”

original.text: Λέγει ⸀αὐτῇ· Ὕπαγε φώνησον ⸂τὸν ἄνδρα σου⸃ καὶ ἐλθὲ ἐνθάδε.

verses.restored: The woman answered and said to him, I do not have a husband. Jesus says to her, You spoke beautifully/well: I do not have a husband.

familiar.text: The woman answered and said, I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, Thou hast well said, I have no husband:

modern.text: “I have no husband,” the woman replied. Jesus said to her, “You are correct to say that you have no husband.

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη ἡ γυνὴ καὶ εἶπεν ⸀αὐτῷ· Οὐκ ἔχω ἄνδρα. λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Καλῶς εἶπας ὅτι Ἄνδρα οὐκ ἔχω·

verses.restored: For you have had five husbands, and the one whom you now have is not your husband; this you have spoken truly.

familiar.text: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly.

modern.text: In fact, you have had five husbands, and the man you now have is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.”

original.text: πέντε γὰρ ἄνδρας ἔσχες, καὶ νῦν ὃν ἔχεις οὐκ ἔστιν σου ἀνήρ· τοῦτο ἀληθὲς εἴρηκας.

verses.restored: The woman says to him, Lord, I behold that you are a prophet.

familiar.text: The woman saith unto him, Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet.

modern.text: “Sir,” the woman said, “I see that You are a prophet.

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή· Κύριε, θεωρῶ ὅτι προφήτης εἶ σύ.

verses.restored: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you say that in Jerusalem is the place where it is necessary to worship.

familiar.text: Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.

modern.text: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem.”

original.text: οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ προσεκύνησαν· καὶ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐστὶν ὁ τόπος ὅπου ⸂προσκυνεῖν δεῖ⸃.

verses.restored: Jesus says to her, Trust me, woman, an hour is coming when neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you worship the Father.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father.

modern.text: “Believe Me, woman,” Jesus replied, “a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.

original.text: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· ⸂Πίστευέ μοι, γύναι⸃, ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ὅτε οὔτε ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ οὔτε ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις προσκυνήσετε τῷ πατρί.

verses.restored: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Judeans.

familiar.text: Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.

modern.text: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we do know, for salvation is from the Jews.

original.text: ὑμεῖς προσκυνεῖτε ὃ οὐκ οἴδατε, ἡμεῖς προσκυνοῦμεν ὃ οἴδαμεν, ὅτι ἡ σωτηρία ἐκ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐστίν·

verses.restored: But an hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in Spirit and truth; for indeed the Father seeks such ones worshiping him.

familiar.text: But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him.

modern.text: But a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such as these to worship Him.

original.text: ἀλλὰ ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν, ὅτε οἱ ἀληθινοὶ προσκυνηταὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ πατρὶ ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ, καὶ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ τοιούτους ζητεῖ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας αὐτόν·

verses.restored: The Divine is Spirit, and those worshiping must worship in Spirit and truth.

familiar.text: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.

modern.text: God is Spirit, and His worshipers must worship Him in spirit and in truth.”

original.text: πνεῦμα ὁ θεός, καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας αὐτὸν ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ δεῖ προσκυνεῖν.

verses.restored: The woman says to him, I know that Messiah is coming, the one called Anointed; when that one comes, he will announce all things to us.

familiar.text: The woman saith unto him, I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things.

modern.text: The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When He comes, He will explain everything to us.”

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ἡ γυνή· Οἶδα ὅτι Μεσσίας ἔρχεται, ὁ λεγόμενος χριστός· ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐκεῖνος, ἀναγγελεῖ ἡμῖν ⸀ἅπαντα.

verses.restored: Jesus says to her, I am, the one speaking to you.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “I who speak to you am He.” The Disciples Return and Marvel

original.text: λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐγώ εἰμι, ὁ λαλῶν σοι.

verses.restored: At this his disciples came and were marveling that he was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, What are you seeking? or, Why are you speaking with her?

familiar.text: And upon this came his disciples, and marvelled that he talked with the woman: yet no man said, What seekest thou? or, Why talkest thou with her?

modern.text: Just then His disciples returned and were surprised that He was speaking with a woman. But no one asked Him, “What do You want from her?” or “Why are You talking with her?”

original.text: Καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἦλθαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ⸀ἐθαύμαζον ὅτι μετὰ γυναικὸς ἐλάλει· οὐδεὶς μέντοι εἶπεν· Τί ζητεῖς; ἢ τί λαλεῖς μετʼ αὐτῆς;

verses.restored: The woman therefore left her water jar, went away into the city, and says to the people,

familiar.text: The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city, and saith to the men,

modern.text: Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town, and said to the people,

original.text: ἀφῆκεν οὖν τὴν ὑδρίαν αὐτῆς ἡ γυνὴ καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις·

verses.restored: Come, see a human who told me all things I did; can this be the Messiah?

familiar.text: Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?

modern.text: “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could this be the Christ?”

original.text: Δεῦτε ἴδετε ἄνθρωπον ὃς εἶπέ μοι πάντα ⸀ὅσα ἐποίησα· μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός;

verses.restored: They went out from the city and were coming to him.

familiar.text: Then they went out of the city, and came unto him.

modern.text: So they left the town and made their way toward Jesus.

original.text: ἐξῆλθον ἐκ τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἤρχοντο πρὸς αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Meanwhile the disciples were asking him, saying, Rabbi, eat.

familiar.text: In the mean while his disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat.

modern.text: Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, “Rabbi, eat something.”

original.text: ⸀Ἐν τῷ μεταξὺ ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Ῥαββί, φάγε.

verses.restored: But he said to them, I have food to eat that you do not know.

familiar.text: But he said unto them, I have meat to eat that ye know not of.

modern.text: But He told them, “I have food to eat that you know nothing about.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐγὼ βρῶσιν ἔχω φαγεῖν ἣν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε.

verses.restored: Therefore the disciples were saying to one another, Did someone bring him something to eat?

familiar.text: Therefore said the disciples one to another, Hath any man brought him ought to eat?

modern.text: So the disciples asked one another, “Could someone have brought Him food?”

original.text: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ μαθηταὶ πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Μή τις ἤνεγκεν αὐτῷ φαγεῖν;

verses.restored: Jesus says to them, My food is that I may do the will of the one who sent me and complete his work.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.

modern.text: Jesus explained, “My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me and to finish His work.

original.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐμὸν βρῶμά ἐστιν ἵνα ⸀ποιήσω τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με καὶ τελειώσω αὐτοῦ τὸ ἔργον.

verses.restored: Do you not say, There are still four months, and then comes the harvest? Look, I say to you, lift up your eyes and behold the fields, that they are white for harvest already.

familiar.text: Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.

modern.text: Do you not say, ‘There are still four months until the harvest’? I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are ripe for harvest.

original.text: οὐχ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι Ἔτι τετράμηνός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ θερισμὸς ἔρχεται; ἰδοὺ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐπάρατε τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν καὶ θεάσασθε τὰς χώρας ὅτι λευκαί εἰσιν πρὸς θερισμόν· ἤδη

verses.restored: The one reaping receives wages and gathers fruit into age-long life, so that the one sowing and the one reaping may rejoice together.

familiar.text: And he that reapeth receiveth wages, and gathereth fruit unto life eternal: that both he that soweth and he that reapeth may rejoice together.

modern.text: Already the reaper draws his wages and gathers a crop for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.

original.text: ⸀ὁ θερίζων μισθὸν λαμβάνει καὶ συνάγει καρπὸν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ⸀ἵνα ὁ σπείρων ὁμοῦ χαίρῃ καὶ ὁ θερίζων.

verses.restored: For in this the word is true: One is sowing and another reaping.

familiar.text: And herein is that saying true, One soweth, and another reapeth.

modern.text: For in this case the saying ‘One sows and another reaps’ is true.

original.text: ἐν γὰρ τούτῳ ὁ λόγος ⸀ἐστὶν ἀληθινὸς ὅτι Ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ σπείρων καὶ ἄλλος ὁ θερίζων·

verses.restored: I sent you to reap what you have not labored for; others have labored, and you have entered into their labor.

familiar.text: I sent you to reap that whereon ye bestowed no labour: other men laboured, and ye are entered into their labours.

modern.text: I sent you to reap what you have not worked for; others have done the hard work, and now you have taken up their labor.” Many Samaritans Believe

original.text: ἐγὼ ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς θερίζειν ὃ οὐχ ὑμεῖς κεκοπιάκατε· ἄλλοι κεκοπιάκασιν, καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν κόπον αὐτῶν εἰσεληλύθατε.

verses.restored: From that city many of the Samaritans trusted into him because of the woman's word bearing witness: He told me all things I did.

familiar.text: And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying of the woman, which testified, He told me all that ever I did.

modern.text: Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s testimony, “He told me everything I ever did.”

original.text: Ἐκ δὲ τῆς πόλεως ἐκείνης πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν τῶν Σαμαριτῶν διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς γυναικὸς μαρτυρούσης ὅτι Εἶπέν μοι πάντα ⸀ἃ ἐποίησα.

verses.restored: When therefore the Samaritans came to him, they were asking him to remain with them; and he remained there two days.

familiar.text: So when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him that he would tarry with them: and he abode there two days.

modern.text: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they asked Him to stay with them, and He stayed two days.

original.text: ὡς οὖν ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Σαμαρῖται, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν μεῖναι παρʼ αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ δύο ἡμέρας.

verses.restored: Many more trusted because of his word.

familiar.text: And many more believed because of his own word;

modern.text: And many more believed because of His message.

original.text: καὶ πολλῷ πλείους ἐπίστευσαν διὰ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: They were saying to the woman, No longer because of your speech do we trust, for we ourselves have heard and know that this one is truly the Savior of the world.

familiar.text: And said unto the woman, Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.

modern.text: They said to the woman, “We now believe not only because of your words; we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this man truly is the Savior of the world.” Jesus Heals the Official’s Son (Matthew 8:5–13; Luke 7:1–10)

original.text: τῇ τε γυναικὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Οὐκέτι διὰ τὴν σὴν λαλιὰν πιστεύομεν· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀκηκόαμεν, καὶ οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ σωτὴρ τοῦ ⸀κόσμου.

verses.restored: After the two days, he went out from there into Galilee.

familiar.text: Now after two days he departed thence, and went into Galilee.

modern.text: After two days, Jesus left for Galilee.

original.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὰς δύο ἡμέρας ἐξῆλθεν ⸀ἐκεῖθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν·

verses.restored: For Jesus himself bore witness that a prophet has no honor in his own homeland.

familiar.text: For Jesus himself testified, that a prophet hath no honour in his own country.

modern.text: Now He Himself had testified that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown.

original.text: αὐτὸς ⸀γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐμαρτύρησεν ὅτι προφήτης ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ πατρίδι τιμὴν οὐκ ἔχει.

verses.restored: When therefore he came into Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all things he did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also went to the feast.

familiar.text: Then when he was come into Galilee, the Galilaeans received him, having seen all the things that he did at Jerusalem at the feast: for they also went unto the feast.

modern.text: Yet when He arrived, the Galileans welcomed Him. They had seen all the great things He had done in Jerusalem at the feast, for they had gone there as well.

original.text: ὅτε οὖν ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν, ἐδέξαντο αὐτὸν οἱ Γαλιλαῖοι, πάντα ἑωρακότες ⸀ὅσα ἐποίησεν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, καὶ αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἦλθον εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν.

verses.restored: He came again to Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. There was a certain royal official whose son was sick in Capernaum.

familiar.text: So Jesus came again into Cana of Galilee, where he made the water wine. And there was a certain nobleman, whose son was sick at Capernaum.

modern.text: So once again He came to Cana in Galilee, where He had turned the water into wine. And there was a royal official whose son lay sick at Capernaum.

original.text: Ἦλθεν οὖν ⸀πάλιν εἰς τὴν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, ὅπου ἐποίησεν τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον. καὶ ἦν τις βασιλικὸς οὗ ὁ υἱὸς ἠσθένει ἐν Καφαρναούμ.

verses.restored: This one, hearing that Jesus had come from Judea into Galilee, went to him and asked that he come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.

familiar.text: When he heard that Jesus was come out of Judaea into Galilee, he went unto him, and besought him that he would come down, and heal his son: for he was at the point of death.

modern.text: When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went and begged Him to come down and heal his son, who was about to die.

original.text: οὗτος ἀκούσας ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἥκει ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ ⸀ἠρώτα ἵνα καταβῇ καὶ ἰάσηται αὐτοῦ τὸν υἱόν, ἤμελλεν γὰρ ἀποθνῄσκειν.

verses.restored: Jesus therefore said to him, Unless you see signs and wonders, you will certainly not trust.

familiar.text: Then said Jesus unto him, Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe.

modern.text: Jesus said to him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe.”

original.text: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἐὰν μὴ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἴδητε, οὐ μὴ πιστεύσητε.

verses.restored: The royal official says to him, Lord, come down before my child dies.

familiar.text: The nobleman saith unto him, Sir, come down ere my child die.

modern.text: “Sir,” the official said, “come down before my child dies.”

original.text: λέγει πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ βασιλικός· Κύριε, κατάβηθι πρὶν ἀποθανεῖν τὸ παιδίον μου.

verses.restored: Jesus says to him, Go; your son lives. The person trusted the word Jesus said to him and went.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto him, Go thy way; thy son liveth. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him, and he went his way.

modern.text: “Go,” said Jesus. “Your son will live.” The man took Jesus at His word and departed.

original.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Πορεύου· ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ. ⸀ἐπίστευσεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ λόγῳ ⸀ὃν εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἐπορεύετο.

verses.restored: Already as he was going down, his servants met him, saying that his child lives.

familiar.text: And as he was now going down, his servants met him, and told him, saying, Thy son liveth.

modern.text: And while he was still on the way, his servants met him with the news that his boy was alive.

original.text: ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ καταβαίνοντος οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ ⸀ὑπήντησαν ⸀αὐτῷ λέγοντες ὅτι ὁ παῖς ⸀αὐτοῦ ζῇ.

verses.restored: He inquired from them the hour in which he became better. They said to him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.

familiar.text: Then enquired he of them the hour when he began to amend. And they said unto him, Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him.

modern.text: So he inquired as to the hour when his son had recovered, and they told him, “The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour. ”

original.text: ἐπύθετο οὖν ⸂τὴν ὥραν παρʼ αὐτῶν⸃ ἐν ᾗ κομψότερον ἔσχεν· ⸂εἶπαν οὖν⸃ αὐτῷ ὅτι ⸀Ἐχθὲς ὥραν ἑβδόμην ἀφῆκεν αὐτὸν ὁ πυρετός.

verses.restored: The father knew that it was at that hour in which Jesus said to him, Your son lives; and he himself trusted, and his whole house.

familiar.text: So the father knew that it was at the same hour, in the which Jesus said unto him, Thy son liveth: and himself believed, and his whole house.

modern.text: Then the father realized that this was the very hour in which Jesus had told him, “Your son will live.” And he and all his household believed.

original.text: ἔγνω οὖν ὁ πατὴρ ⸀ὅτι ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐν ᾗ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ ⸀Ἰησοῦς· Ὁ υἱός σου ζῇ, καὶ ἐπίστευσεν αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ οἰκία αὐτοῦ ὅλη.

verses.restored: This again, a second sign, Jesus did after coming from Judea into Galilee.

familiar.text: This is again the second miracle that Jesus did, when he was come out of Judaea into Galilee.

modern.text: This was now the second sign that Jesus performed after coming from Judea into Galilee.

original.text: τοῦτο ⸀δὲ πάλιν δεύτερον σημεῖον ἐποίησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλθὼν ἐκ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν.
